newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli blast separates mother and baby.
newsitem.headline: Israeli blast separates mother and baby.

text.p: An Israeli policewoman cradled a baby girl in her arms.
Hopelessly the woman looked left and right for the crying infant's parents. The baby wore the tatters of a clown costume for the Jewish Purim festival.
But the mother was in no condition to care for the child.
"I saw her mother," medic Pinni Melech told Israel Radio. "Her whole face was burned, without an ear and a mess."
Both mother and child were rushed to Tel Aviv's Ichilov hospital -- the baby to intensive care. The hospital would not comment on the mother's fate.

A sunny day that drew crowds to Tel Aviv's sidewalks turned to darkness with a suicide-bomb blast that ripped through a cafe in the country's metropolitan heart, killing four people, including the bomber.
There was blood on the sidewalk at the Apropos sidewalk cafe where the explosion occurred. Unfinished meals on the tables. The smell of charred flesh in the air.
It was a festive Friday mid-afternoon, the end of the work week, the eve of the Jewish sabbath.
Schools were out and children had joined their parents.
So joyous a day was it in fact that the wounded baby wore a costume -- a traditional part of the Purim holiday this weekend marking the salvation of Jews from genocide in ancient Persia.
"They want to ruin another Purim for us," shouted Israeli onlookers after the blast.
Only last Purim, a Palestinian suicide bomber turned a Tel Aviv street into a scene of horror, blowing himself up and killing 13 people.
Israel's former U.N. Ambassador Gad Yaacobi happened to be there this time.
"We were inside the cafe. There was a huge blast that threw us back. Glass. We looked at the garden and saw the whole garden destroyed and dozens of people lying on the ground," he told reporters.
Waitress Iris Gan said: "Everyone began to run."
Afterwards witnesses said they had noticed a suspicious man walk in carrying a big yellow dufflebag minutes before the explosion.
"When I think back, a guy came in who looked like one of us with a big bag and sat with it next to him at a table," a man told Israel Radio.
"I paid attention because he was out of the ordinary," witness Dafna Alon said. "He picked the 'best' place to sit."
Afterwards she saw his bloodied body. Workers picked the body up and removed it in a bag.

Israeli security forces had been on high alert expecting Palestinian violence, including suicide attacks, in protest at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's groundbreaking for the Jewish settlement this week in Arab East Jerusalem.
Scores of Israelis angry about the explosion turned up afterwards. "Terrorism will not triumph" read one of their protest signs.
"We've come here to back up the prime minister," Israeli Nissim Cohen said.
